syntheticNotes:
SYNTHETIC — NOT A REAL BILL. Exists so the fixture harness is runnable before real bills arrive. Delete or ignore it once real fixtures land.

Every number below was computed BY HAND from fixtures/tariffs/synthetic-gs2-like-2026-06-01.json, not read off the engine — a fixture generated from the engine would only prove the engine equals itself.

Derivation. July 2026 has 31 days, no DST transition, so 31 x 96 = 2976 quarter-hours. The load is flat at 2 kWh per quarter-hour, hence 5952 kWh and a constant 8 kW.

July 1 2026 is a Wednesday, giving 23 weekdays and 8 weekend days. July 3 is the observed Independence Day (July 4 falls on a Saturday) and the tariff rates holidays on the Sunday schedule, so it moves from weekday to weekend treatment: 22 weekday-treated days and 9 weekend-treated days.

  on-peak   22 d x 5 h x 4 x 2 kWh =  880 kWh @ 0.32 =  281.60
  mid-peak   9 d x 5 h x 4 x 2 kWh =  360 kWh @ 0.22 =   79.20
  off-peak  5952 - 880 - 360       = 4712 kWh @ 0.12 =  565.44
  facilities demand   2 kWh / 0.25 h = 8 kW   @ 18.50 = 148.00
  customer charge                     31 days @  1.20 =  37.20
  public purpose                    5952 kWh @ 0.015 =   89.28
                                     stage 0-4 subtotal 1200.72
  utility users tax                  8% of 1200.72   =   96.06
                                                total   1296.78
label: Synthetic July 2026 bill, flat 8 kW load, facilities-only schedule

source.notes: There is no bill PDF because there is no bill. A real fixture must name the scan it was transcribed from.
